description: Shared Proxmox Backup Server (PBS) contract fixture between fivenines-agent and fivenines-server. Source of truth: fivenines-agent tests/fixtures/pbs_contract_payload.json, asserted end-to-end by tests/test_pbs.py::test_contract_fixture_round_trip (only the HTTP transport is mocked: each scenario's recorded responses replay through the real collector). The server keeps a BYTE-IDENTICAL copy and posts each scenario's payload under data['pbs']; change the shape only in lockstep. Responses marked CAPTURED were recorded from a real PBS 4.2.0 on 2026-09-28 with the official proxmox-backup-client 4.2.6 producing the backups; SYNTHETIC ones are derived and say so. A scenario with `responses_base` replays that scenario's responses with its own `responses` on top; one with `agent_state` starts from that agent state (walks_held: an earlier build of the agent armed the walk hold). Every scenario is an independent build with the same frozen built_at: replay them one by one, never as consecutive builds.
_agent_min_version_note: First agent release carrying the pbs collector. Purely config-driven: an older agent ignores the top-level 'pbs' key entirely (the key is absent from its payload), so the server may send it before the fleet upgrades.

config_contract._note: config['pbs'] is a TOP-LEVEL key, never nested under config['proxmox'] (that dict is splatted into proxmox_metrics(**kwargs), where a new key would TypeError every older agent). It is splatted into pbs_metrics(**config['pbs']), which takes **_kwargs, so a key added later is ignored by this agent rather than breaking it. Push a given PBS to ONE agent (the one on the PBS itself, by default): the walk hold that caps a stuck namespace walk at one pinned PBS proxy thread lives in each agent's memory, so N agents polling the same PBS can pin N threads (errors_contract.backoff). An agent pointed at another PBS keeps a walk hold armed by the previous one until it is reloaded (SIGHUP) or restarted (field_contract.walks_held).
config_contract.host: PBS API host. Default 'localhost': the agent installed on the PBS itself; null or '' also mean the default. A hostname or an IP literal only (no scheme, path, port or userinfo) -- anything else is a config_error. With verification off, the NAME localhost is dialled as 127.0.0.1 (a name resolves through NSS and, without an /etc/hosts entry, DNS).
config_contract.port: Default 8007; null or '' also mean the default.
config_contract.token_id: An API TOKEN id, 'user@realm!tokenname' (printable ASCII). A user/password login is not supported (a ticket login is a far wider credential).
config_contract.token_secret: The token secret (printable ASCII, no whitespace). Never part of any cache key, and removed from every error message before it is logged or shipped.
config_contract.verify_ssl: Verify the certificate against the bundled public CA set (requests' certifi bundle; the OS trust store and REQUESTS_CA_BUNDLE are NOT consulted). Default true; only an explicit false (false/0/'false'/'no'/'off') disables it. A certificate from an internal CA therefore needs `fingerprint`.
config_contract.fingerprint: SHA-256 certificate fingerprint to PIN instead (as shown by PBS: Dashboard > Show Fingerprint, or proxmox-backup-manager cert info), with or without colons, any case. The Proxmox-native way to trust PBS's default self-signed certificate. A pin names ONE certificate: after a renewal the tls_error envelope carries the new one in presented_fingerprint. When set, verify_ssl is irrelevant.
config_contract.tls_policy: The token is NEVER sent over unverified TLS to a non-loopback host: a remote host needs verify_ssl true or a fingerprint, else config_error before any request. verify_ssl false with no fingerprint is accepted for loopback only (localhost, 127.0.0.0/8, ::1); pinning is recommended there too. Proxy and netrc environment variables are ignored, and redirects are refused.

privilege_contract._note: Measured on PBS 4.2: a token's effective privileges are the INTERSECTION of its user's ACL and its own ACL, so BOTH need the grant. PBS HIDES what a token may not audit instead of refusing it (HTTP 200, empty list), which is why the agent reads /access/permissions ({path: {privilege: propagate}}) first.
privilege_contract.setup: proxmox-backup-manager user create fivenines@pbs; proxmox-backup-manager user generate-token fivenines@pbs monitoring; then for BOTH auth ids 'fivenines@pbs' and 'fivenines@pbs!monitoring': proxmox-backup-manager acl update /datastore DatastoreAudit --auth-id <id>; proxmox-backup-manager acl update /remote RemoteAudit --auth-id <id>
privilege_contract.read_only_rule: The token may hold Datastore.Audit and Remote.Audit and NOTHING else. Any other effective privilege -> over_privileged envelope, nothing collected: Datastore.Read (restore every backup), Datastore.Backup/Prune/Modify/Verify, Sys.Modify, Permissions.Modify, Remote.Read, ... and also Sys.Audit (it reads the PBS system journal and syslog) and Tape.Audit (unused).
privilege_contract.measured_roles: CAPTURED from GET /access/roles on PBS 4.2.0: DatastoreAudit = [Datastore.Audit]; RemoteAudit = [Remote.Audit]; Audit = [Sys.Audit, Datastore.Audit]; DatastoreReader = [Datastore.Audit, Datastore.Read, Datastore.Verify]; DatastoreBackup = [Datastore.Backup]; DatastorePowerUser = [Datastore.Backup, Datastore.Prune]. Only DatastoreAudit and RemoteAudit pass the read-only rule; a token given the built-in Audit role is refused.
privilege_contract.propagation: CAPTURED: a DatastoreAudit ACL on /datastore with propagate OFF shows as {'/datastore': {'Datastore.Audit': false}} and reaches no datastore (every listing is an empty 200). Only a PROPAGATED Datastore.Audit reaching /datastore counts as seeing every datastore (a grant on / is reported AT /datastore, inherited: PBS always evaluates /datastore and /remote, and omits a path only when the token has no privilege there -- so / with /datastore absent means an entry at /datastore hid every datastore, and reads no_datastore_access); a grant on /datastore/<store>[/<ns>] is a scoped token; neither -> no_datastore_access. A scoped token whose grants reach no existing datastore -> no_datastore_access too.
privilege_contract.remote_audit: Sync jobs are listed only with a PROPAGATED Remote.Audit reaching /remote (granted there or on /, which PBS reports at /remote, inherited). Without it sync_jobs is null plus a 'sync_jobs' error naming the privilege.
privilege_contract.scoped_token: Datastore.Audit granted below /datastore (one datastore or one namespace) is accepted, but PBS then hides every job defined outside that scope: each job list read under such a token carries a 'partial:' error under its own scope.
privilege_contract.deeper_acls: Verified in PBS source (pbs-config acl.rs): an ACL entry deeper in the tree REPLACES the roles inherited from above at that path, it does not add to them. So an entry below /datastore or /remote on the token or its user whose role lacks the audited privilege (Datastore.Audit, Remote.Audit under /remote) -- NoAccess, a RemoteAudit, or e.g. a DatastoreBackup the user also holds for PVE backups -- leaves the token (token ACL intersected with user ACL) without that privilege there, and PBS hides that datastore, namespace or remote without an error. /access/permissions then lists the path WITHOUT the audited privilege when the role grants another one (measured on PBS 4.2: a RemoteAudit entry on /datastore/store1 reads Remote.Audit there, and store1 drops out of the datastore listing), lists it NOT propagated when the user holds the audited role without propagation next to a role that does propagate (measured: DatastoreAudit, propagate off, beside DatastoreBackup on /datastore/store1 reads Datastore.Audit false there, and store1's namespaces drop out while store1 itself stays audited), and leaves it out when the role grants nothing (NoAccess) -- measured: a non-propagated NoAccess on /datastore/store1/clusterA hides clusterA from the namespace listing and from /access/permissions, while clusterA/sub, which is not an ACL node, inherits Datastore.Audit past it and stays listed. The setup therefore uses a DEDICATED user with no other ACL. The agent detects a violation BELOW /datastore or /remote when the map shows it: a path without the audited privilege, a path holding it NOT propagated (also a harmless non-propagated entry, which the map cannot tell apart: reported partial), or a path under an absent one (the token still audits a path below the entry); and, outside the map, when a namespace listing names a namespace whose parent it does not list. Below /datastore, scope is then 'partial' and the three job lists 'partial:'; below /remote, sync_jobs 'partial:' only. An entry leaving the token nothing at a path, with no ACL entry of the token or its user below it, stays undetectable (measured: a non-propagated NoAccess on /datastore/<store> drops the datastore whole, although its namespaces still inherit Datastore.Audit); the job lists are flagged 'partial:' in any build where a datastore's namespaces were not read, since a hidden namespace shows only there; an entry AT /datastore or /remote hiding a grant made on / is detected: no_datastore_access, or sync_jobs null.

envelope_contract: data['pbs'] is never null. FAILURE: exactly {reachable, error_type, error_message}, plus presented_fingerprint when error_type is tls_error, and NO 'datastores' key -> the server ingests nothing and prunes nothing. SUCCESS: {reachable: true, scope, version, release, fingerprint, age_s, built_at, walks_held, datastores, groups, sync_jobs, verify_jobs, prune_jobs, errors}. Branch on the presence of 'datastores' (or of 'error_type'). reachable is true whenever /version answered this tick, so a rebuild that fails later (a read timing out) is a slow or broken PBS, not an unreachable one.

error_types.config_error: Invalid host/port/token/fingerprint, or the TLS policy refused the target. reachable false; nothing was sent.
error_types.connection_refused: Connection refused / DNS failure / no route. reachable false.
error_types.timeout: Connect or read timeout, or the tick's 20s budget ran out (message 'skipped: pbs collection deadline exceeded'). reachable is true when /version answered this tick. A collection still running after the hard 30s bound (resolving the host name, connecting to its addresses, or a PBS that stopped answering) is abandoned: error_type timeout, reachable true only if its /version had answered; every later tick reports the same timeout, reachable included, until it returns, whatever the config says meanwhile (no second collection starts).
error_types.tls_error: Certificate verification failed or the pinned fingerprint did not match. reachable false; the token was not sent. presented_fingerprint: the SHA-256 of the certificate WHATEVER answered on host:port presented, from a bare TLS handshake (no request, no token), or null when that handshake failed too. It is UNVERIFIED by construction -- a man in the middle, or a local listener while the PBS proxy is down, presents its own -- so it is a hint to compare with `proxmox-backup-manager cert info` on the PBS console, never a value to trust or apply automatically.
error_types.auth_failed: HTTP 401 (wrong, disabled or deleted token). reachable true. The agent then leaves the PBS alone for 300s (each attempt is an authentication failure in the PBS auth log) unless the secret changes, and keeps reporting this envelope meanwhile.
error_types.http_error: Any other failure of a read the whole block depends on (/version, /access/permissions, /admin/datastore): a non-200, a malformed or oversized body. reachable true if PBS answered. Also a block too large to ship -- over 8 MB of JSON or 1 MB gzipped; it is re-emitted every tick, and a real block at every cap is ~3 MB of JSON, ~0.1 MB gzipped, so only a broken PBS gets there; that envelope is cached for the TTL like a block -- and the catch-all for anything unexpected, such as a collection whose thread could not start (reachable false).
error_types.over_privileged: The token holds a privilege beyond Datastore.Audit and Remote.Audit. reachable true.
error_types.no_datastore_access: The token can audit no datastore (no grant, or one without propagation, or a scoped grant reaching no existing datastore). reachable true.

freshness: The block (scope, datastores, groups, jobs, errors, walks_held) is rebuilt at most once per 300s and re-emitted, identical, with age_s = seconds since it was built (anchor freshness as received_at - age_s) and built_at = the agent's epoch seconds when it was built: every re-emission carries the SAME built_at and a rebuild a new one, so built_at is the build's identity (a block is re-emitted ~5 times per TTL; count builds, never payloads). /version, fingerprint and reachability are read EVERY tick: a PBS that goes down produces the failure envelope on the next tick, not after the TTL. A failed build is not cached (a block too large to ship is: its envelope is re-emitted for the TTL). One tick of this collector (/version plus a rebuild) works within a 20s budget that also clamps every request's timeouts, so it stays NEAR that bound (what no request timeout covers -- resolving the host name, connecting to each of its addresses -- is cut by a hard 30s bound). After the block-level reads (usage status, datastore config, job lists), a build reads in three steps. (1) The namespace walks: a datastore's namespace listing is sent only with its whole 10s read timeout left in the tick, and past the first walk of the build only with 4s more beyond that, so the reads after them always keep some time. (2) Each datastore's own status and gc, within half of what the walks left (plus up to 5s: an own status or gc read sent with that much of the half left, as one of the first datastore's two reads, or retried after a timeout waits at least 5s, so its timeout means PBS did not answer, and an answer that comes within that wait is read). (3) The group reads, until the budget is spent. The group reads go only through the namespaces of the datastores walked IN THE SAME BUILD, so every namespace they read whole was listed in that build -- the only builds where its groups can be authoritative (pruning_contract). The walks start at the datastore where the group reads stand and go round the datastores until their time is up or the namespace cap (1000, a total over the build's listings) is full; the group reads then resume where they stopped. When one build cannot read everything, the next resumes at the first namespace the group reads cut (the budget or the group cap ran out inside its read, or before it was started; a read that merely failed is not a cut) -- or past it when it was already the first of the build -- and, when none was cut, at the datastore where the walks stopped. The own status and gc reads keep their own position the same way: they resume at the first datastore whose gc the half cut, or past it when it was the first. When the walks did not go round every datastore, the group reads never wrap back into the earlier namespaces of the datastore they resumed in (a 'groups' errors[] entry names them: read on its next turn). Each build with time for a step therefore either reads all of it or moves on by at least one item (a namespace, or a datastore for the gc reads): every namespace is reached within as many builds as there are namespaces, and a PBS too big for one build is read in rounds of several builds. The position is kept by name, not by place: a datastore or namespace added or removed in between does not shift it (one that is gone resumes at the next in sort order). A datastore where a read in its namespaces timed out (its namespace walk, a groups or a snapshot listing) is not read further until a walk lists it again: the rest of its namespaces that build stay unread, with a 'groups' errors[] entry. While the walk hold is on (walks_held), no walk is sent, and the group reads go through the namespace listings the agent remembers from earlier builds instead (at most 1000 namespaces in all; never a datastore whose read timed out since its last listing): those groups ship as current data, but every namespaces is null, so none is authoritative. After an agent reload, the reads resume just past the datastore whose walk armed the hold, and that datastore -- with any whose walk armed the hold before an earlier reload -- is walked only once the group reads reach it: every other datastore is walked and its namespaces read before it can arm the hold again (until then the walks of a build stop there, errors_contract.namespaces, and the job lists read 'partial:'). A datastore repaired without a proxy restart is therefore walked again up to one round of the group reads after the reload.

field_contract.version / release: /version verbatim (e.g. '4.2' / '0'). PBS spells its version as version = MAJOR.MINOR and release = the PATCH level: PBS 4.0.17 answers version '4.0', release '17', so the full version is version + '.' + release -- NOT Proxmox VE's convention (PVE ships version '8.2.4'). Every version gate in this contract (4.0.17, 4.1.6, 4.1.7) is on the full version.
field_contract.fingerprint: SHA-256 of the certificate the PBS presented on this tick's connection, lowercase colon form; the pinned fingerprint when the socket could not be read (e.g. a reverse proxy answering Connection: close); null when neither is known. The join key with the PVE side (see pve_join_contract).
field_contract.built_at: Integer epoch seconds (the agent's clock) when this block was built. Every re-emission of a cached block carries the same value and a rebuild a new one: it is the build's identity, which the pruning rule counts -- compare it for EQUALITY only (distinct built_at values, never payloads). It is not an ordering key: the agent's clock can step back (NTP, a manual fix); order payloads by queue order or received_at - age_s.
field_contract.walks_held: true once a namespace walk timed out and every walk is held (the namespace listings and the usage status share ONE hold, released only by an agent reload or restart). From the next build on, no namespace listing is read: every datastore's namespaces is null and every job list read carries a 'partial:' flag -- nothing was listed, not 'nothing exists'. The group reads go on through the namespace listings the agent remembers from earlier builds (freshness): those groups ship as current data, none authoritative (namespaces null: pruning_contract). The build that armed the hold may still carry the datastores read before the timeout, and their rows follow the usual rules. While it is true, treat every group already stored for this PBS and not shipped in this block as of UNKNOWN freshness (no overdue or stale alert, never 'no backups'), estimated_full_date reads null (unknown, as always: datastores[]), and ALERT the operator now: the stuck walk is a busy loop on a PBS core that logs an error each turn until proxmox-backup-proxy restarts -- repair the storage, restart proxmox-backup-proxy, then reload the agent. It is the AGENT's state, not only this PBS's: an agent moved to another PBS keeps a hold armed by the previous one until it is reloaded (config_contract), so the alert names the agent too. false otherwise; absent on an agent older than this field.
field_contract.datastores[]: One per datastore the token can audit, sorted by store: store, backend_type ('filesystem' | 's3' ...; from the listing on PBS >= 4.1.7, the usage status on 4.1.6, else /config/datastore, where no backend property means 'filesystem'; null = unknown, and then the usage fields are null too), mount_status ('nonremovable' | 'mounted' | 'notmounted'), maintenance_mode ('read-only' | 'offline' | ... | null) + maintenance_message (capped 200), total/used/avail (bytes; NULL when unknown, never 0; for a full-scope token from /status/datastore-usage, or -- when that read fails as a whole, which PBS does when ONE datastore's statfs errors, or is held -- from each datastore's own status, then without estimated_full_date; a SCOPED token never reads /status/datastore-usage (PBS walks, to answer it, every datastore the token cannot audit, visible or not): a datastore it audits at the datastore level reports its own status, without estimated_full_date, and one it audits only below reads null; always NULL for a non-filesystem backend such as 's3', where PBS measures its local CACHE disk), estimated_full_date (epoch, PBS's own forecast verbatim; null is UNKNOWN whatever the cause -- no history yet, a non-filesystem backend (whose forecast is of the local cache disk), a usage read from the datastore's own status (the usage status failed or is held, or a scoped token), the walk hold -- and never resolves a filling-up incident; 0 is its 'no fill expected' sentinel for flat usage, and also what an unforecastable history gives; a date in the past means usage is shrinking; a nearly flat datastore can give a date far past any calendar, up to 9223372036854775807 -- read anything beyond a sane horizon as 'not in the foreseeable future', never as a timestamp to store as is), gc, namespaces, unread_namespaces.
field_contract.datastores[].gc: {schedule, next_run, last_run_starttime, last_run_state (verbatim: 'OK', 'WARNINGS: n' or an error), last_run_endtime, duration, index_file_count, index_data_bytes, disk_bytes, disk_chunks, pending_bytes, pending_chunks, removed_bytes, removed_chunks, removed_bad, still_bad}, or null when unread (failed, skipped past the budget, or backed off after a timeout: errors_contract.backoff). PBS keeps a GC's status only when the run SUCCEEDS: last_run_starttime (from its task id) and the counters describe the last successful GC; last_run_state and last_run_endtime the last run, whatever its outcome. So: all null = no successful GC known (it may have run and failed); a start time with a null state = a PBS older than ~3.2 (which reports no state) or a GC running now; a failed state next to an older start time = the last run failed, and duration then spans from that older start. Dedup factor = index_data_bytes / disk_bytes.
field_contract.datastores[].namespaces: The namespaces the token can see, sorted ('' = root). NULL when the namespace set is unknown: its listing failed, a row of it could not be parsed, it was not sent this build (the budget ran out first, the walk hold: walks_held, the walks stopped at a datastore whose walk armed the hold before an agent reload: errors_contract.namespaces, or the namespace cap was full: 'cap' errors[] entry 'namespaces capped at 1000: not read'), or it did not fit the namespace cap -- a total over the build's listings (1000): a listing that does not fit ends that build's walks -- dropped whole although it was read, with the same 'namespaces capped at 1000: not read' entry, since none of its namespaces is read that build -- and is listed first in a later one, and one that does not fit even as the first listing of a build is kept trimmed, its namespaces kept still read ('cap' entry 'namespaces capped at 1000: N dropped'), so which datastore goes null moves between builds. A null namespaces says nothing about the datastore's health: only a listing that was SENT and failed carries a 'namespaces' errors[] entry with PBS's own message (a budget skip or the hold carries the 'deadline' or 'backoff' message instead).
field_contract.datastores[].unread_namespaces: The namespaces of `namespaces` whose GROUPS are unknown this build: their /groups read failed or is backed off after a timeout, a group row could not be parsed, their /snapshots did not come back as a list (an HTTP error, a timeout, a reset, a budget skip, a backoff or an unreadable body: PBS leaves out of /groups a group whose snapshots it failed to read, and only /snapshots fails on it), the group cap trimmed or never reached them, the budget ran out first, a read in that datastore's namespaces timed out first in this build ('groups' errors[] entry 'skipped: a read on this datastore timed out in this build, so the rest of its namespaces wait for a later one', followed by the count of namespaces not read), or -- when the walks did not go round every datastore -- they lie before the point the group reads resumed at in their datastore, and the round has not come back to them ('groups' errors[] entry 'skipped: before the resume point of this build in its datastore, read on its next turn'). Every listed namespace not read whole in this build is in it, whatever the reason. NULL whenever namespaces is null. A build where a namespace is listed here counts toward no absence of its groups, and any group it does ship still resets that group's count (pruning_contract).
field_contract.groups[]: One per backup group (store, ns, type 'vm'|'ct'|'host', id), sorted. last_backup: the newest FINISHED backup (/groups last-backup, discarded when /groups names a snapshot with no manifest -- PBS does so for a group whose only snapshot is still uploading; a snapshot still uploading can never be it; null when the group has none -- BUT when in_progress is null (the snapshot listing was not read) on PBS < 4.0.17, last_backup is a LOWER BOUND: that PBS's /groups folds over an unsorted listing, so while an upload runs it can name an older backup, or the upload itself (discarded -> null), and must never read as 'no backup' or 'overdue'; when the snapshot listing was read, its newest finished snapshot wins if /groups gives none OR an older one -- PBS < 4.0.17 folds last-backup over an unsorted listing; before 4.0.17 a group with no snapshot at all is absent from /groups rather than listed with last-backup 0). count: PBS backup-count verbatim (it includes a snapshot still uploading). in_progress: a snapshot newer than last_backup has no manifest yet; in_progress_since: that snapshot's BACKUP time (null unless in_progress), not when writing started -- a long backup keeps its start time, a pull sync writes the SOURCE's backup time (days old while the sync is live), and PBS keeps an upload orphaned by a crash, so age alone cannot tell a dead upload from a live one. What can depends on who uploads: a PULL sync has a job row here (last_run_starttime set, last_run_state null while it runs); a PVE backup has none on this PBS, its running vzdump task is on the PVE host, lined up through the pbs join key of the PVE storage row; a proxmox-backup-client upload, or a sync PUSHED here by another PBS, leaves nothing a read-only token can see, so there the same in_progress_since persisting well past the group's usual backup duration is the only sign of an orphan -- and in_progress NULL means every snapshot detail of the row is unknown (the snapshot listing was not read, or it did not show last_backup finished). size: bytes of the last_backup snapshot. crypt_mode: 'encrypt' | 'sign-only' | 'none' | 'mixed' (from its archives; the manifest is ignored). protected. Every verification field counts ONLY verifications that ran on THIS datastore (an 'ok' one also on a node of THIS PBS, see below): a pull sync copies each snapshot's manifest verbatim, verification state included, so a synced copy carries its SOURCE's verification (another datastore, often another PBS), which PBS's verify jobs then skip by default (ignore-verified); the agent checks the verify task id (its worker id starts with the datastore, its node must be one this PBS's own GC/job task ids carry, when any is known -- else only the datastore name is checked). The node check applies to an 'ok' only: a 'failed' verification of this datastore counts whatever node ran it (a PBS renamed or reinstalled keeps its own past verifications under the old node name; a copied failure is at worst a false alarm, a hidden real one is missed corruption), and after such a rename an 'ok' reads never-verified-here until PBS verifies the snapshot again. On a pull-sync TARGET, every sync run re-pulls the newest snapshot and renames the source's manifest over it, erasing a local verification of that snapshot, failed included: verify_failed_count dropping (1 -> 0) on a synced group is NOT proof of a repair (the sync job's resync-corrupt option re-downloads a snapshot that failed verification). A heuristic, not proof: nodes compare by NAME, and the sync source writes the copied task id, so a source PBS with the same node and datastore name is indistinguishable. verify_state: 'ok' | 'failed' | null (never verified HERE, when in_progress is not null) of the last_backup snapshot; verify_time: when that verification ran (from its task id). last_verified_ok: backup time of the newest snapshot that verified OK here -- the newest restore point known to be intact on this datastore. verify_failed_count: snapshots in the group whose last local verification failed.
field_contract.sync_jobs[]: Sorted by (store, id). id, store, ns, max_depth, schedule, next_run, last_run_starttime, last_run_state (verbatim), last_run_endtime, remote (null = a local sync), remote_store, remote_ns, direction ('pull' | 'push'). The roles swap with direction: a PULL job copies remote/remote_store/remote_ns INTO store/ns on this PBS (store is the target); a PUSH job copies store/ns FROM this PBS to remote/remote_store/remote_ns (store is the source). Push jobs (PBS >= 3.3) are included. max_depth null = full recursion (0 = this namespace only), in all three job lists. For every job list: last_run_starttime comes from the last run's task id; a job RUNNING now has it set with a null state and end time (a sync hung for days shows its start); all three null = never ran, or its state is unknown.
field_contract.verify_jobs[]: Sorted by (store, id). id, store, ns, max_depth, schedule, next_run, last_run_starttime, last_run_state, last_run_endtime, outdated_after (days), ignore_verified (absent from PBS's config = true, its default).
field_contract.prune_jobs[]: Sorted by (store, id). id, store, ns, max_depth, schedule, next_run, last_run_starttime, last_run_state, last_run_endtime, disabled.
field_contract.never_shipped: Owners, comments/notes, file lists, encryption-key fingerprints, task ids, the token secret. Every shipped string is UTF-8-sanitized, NUL-free and capped (500 chars; maintenance_message 200); error messages are also redacted.
field_contract.scope: 'full' when the token audits every datastore (a propagated Datastore.Audit reaching /datastore) and no datastore was trimmed by the cap -- except what a deeper ACL entry hides, which shows only when /access/permissions lists the hidden path without Datastore.Audit, with it not propagated, or lists a path below it, or when a namespace listing names a namespace without its parent -- then 'partial' (privilege_contract.deeper_acls), hence the two-absences rule in pruning_contract; else 'partial': a datastore, namespace or group ABSENT from this block may exist and simply be invisible to the token, so nothing is pruned from a partial block (every job list it carries is flagged 'partial:' too).

pruning_contract: What may be pruned is carried OUTSIDE errors[] (which is capped) -- except a job list's completeness: a list that was read but may be partial is flagged by a 'partial:' errors[] entry under its own scope, placed ahead of every entry from the per-datastore and per-namespace READS (namespace listings, own status, gc, groups, snapshots): only a bounded prefix (the datastore-cap entry, the usage status's entries (its own failure or hold, or one per listed datastore), the datastore_config entry and the job lists' own entries (a failure, or a 'partial:' entry for capped or unparseable rows), far under the cap) can come before it, so the cap never drops it. An unparseable row makes its scope unknown, never smaller -- including a datastore, namespace or group whose name is outside PBS's own schema (a datastore or namespace level is a safe id [A-Za-z0-9_][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,254}, a namespace at most 500 characters -- the wire cap, so no two ship alike -- and a group (vm|ct|host)/safe id): a real PBS never sends one. A group row is authoritative for its (store, ns) ONLY when scope is 'full', that datastore's namespaces is not null and ns is listed in namespaces but NOT in unread_namespaces -- and groups absent there are gone. Under 'partial' no group is ever authoritative: where the token lacks Datastore.Audit but holds Datastore.Backup (a deeper entry the map may not show), PBS lists only the groups the token OWNS, with HTTP 200 and no error, so a namespace read under a partial scope can be short. A namespace absent from a non-null namespaces list is gone with its groups, and a datastore absent from datastores is gone -- but ONLY when scope is 'full'; under 'partial' an absent datastore or namespace is not visible to this token, never gone. A datastore with namespaces null, or a namespace in unread_namespaces: nothing may be pruned there (rows shipped are still current). Nor may it raise an overdue or stale alert: a group stored earlier for such a datastore or namespace and not shipped in this build keeps its last stored values with UNKNOWN freshness -- the namespace can stay unread for many builds (a listing that keeps failing or is backed off up to 6h, the budget, a cap, the walk hold) -- so alert on 'not read for N consecutive builds' instead, never on its stale last_backup. An ACL entry below /datastore or /remote on the monitoring token or its user whose role lacks the audited privilege (a deeper entry REPLACES the inherited role: a NoAccess, a RemoteAudit on a datastore, a DatastoreBackup the user also holds, or the audited role without propagation next to one that propagates) makes PBS hide that path from the token: that datastore, namespace or remote's sync jobs then vanish from a block that would read scope 'full' unless the agent detects the entry (below). PBS leaves the path out of /access/permissions only where the token holds NO privilege there. The setup forbids such entries. The agent detects one when it shows in /access/permissions: a path listed WITHOUT the audited privilege (measured on PBS 4.2: a RemoteAudit entry on /datastore/<store> makes that path read Remote.Audit, and PBS stops listing the datastore), a path listing it NOT propagated (measured: the user's DatastoreAudit without propagation beside a propagated DatastoreBackup reads Datastore.Audit false there, and every namespace below is hidden -- a harmless non-propagated entry reads the same and is reported partial too), or a path listed under an absent one (the token still audits a path below the entry); and one the map does NOT show when a namespace listing names a namespace without its parent (measured: a non-propagated NoAccess on <store>/<ns> hides <ns> from the listing and from /access/permissions, while the namespaces below it, which are not ACL nodes, stay listed). Below /datastore the block then reads scope 'partial' and every job list carries a 'partial:' flag, and a datastore hidden at its own level is either absent or listed with its usage null, never the 0/0/0 its own status answers (a 0/0/0 own status always reads unknown); below /remote only sync_jobs carries a 'partial:' flag (scope is untouched). Since a namespace listing is the only way to see the last case, every job list read also carries a 'partial:' flag in any build where some datastore's namespaces were not read (its listing failed, was held, or was not requested for the budget or a full namespace cap, or the datastore is past the 100-datastore cap; a listing read but not kept under the cap counts as read: it was scanned whole for a hidden namespace): unknown, never complete -- so no job is pruned on a PBS whose walks do not go round every datastore in one build, while walks_held, on a PBS with more than 100 datastores, or while a datastore is in offline maintenance or a removable datastore is unplugged (PBS refuses its namespace listing for as long as that lasts). An entry that leaves the token NO privilege at a path, with no ACL entry of the token or its user below it, stays invisible (measured: a non-propagated NoAccess on /datastore/<store> drops the datastore whole -- from the listing and from /access/permissions -- although its namespaces still inherit Datastore.Audit from /datastore; the block reads scope 'full'). PBS ITSELF leaves out of its 200 answers a group it failed to read and a namespace whose iteration failed. For a group whose snapshot directory cannot be read, /snapshots fails (HTTP 400, once its scan reaches that group) and the agent marks the namespace unread -- and since a /snapshots that timed out, or did not come back as a list, gives no such signal, it marks the namespace unread too. A group whose OWNER file cannot be read is left out of /groups AND /snapshots with 200 (PBS only logs a warning): invisible to the agent, for as long as the file stays unreadable. While walks_held is true, no namespace or group of this PBS that the block does not carry is authoritative for pruning, and the stored ones are of unknown freshness (field_contract.walks_held); datastores and gc keep their usual rules, and the job lists carry their 'partial:' flags (no namespace listing is read). Absence is strong evidence, not proof: prune a datastore, namespace or group only after it has been absent from TWO successful BUILDS where its scope was authoritative, with no build in between that ships it -- two distinct built_at values; a re-emission of the same block (same built_at) is not a second absence. A build where its scope is NOT authoritative (for a group: the scope partial, its datastore's namespaces null, or its namespace not listed or in unread_namespaces; for a namespace: the scope partial or its datastore's namespaces null; for a datastore: the scope partial) neither counts nor resets the count -- on a PBS too big for one build the reads come back to a namespace only every few builds, possibly several builds apart -- while ANY build that ships it, authoritative or not, resets the count. Treat one that vanished while its PBS stayed reachable as worth surfacing, not only as deleted.

errors_contract._note: errors[] = {scope, store, ns, message}, capped at 500 entries: diagnostic detail for what was not read. Entries are appended in read order -- except the job lists' scope, ACL and namespace-listing 'partial:' flags, placed ahead of every entry from the per-datastore and per-namespace reads (only the datastore-cap entry, the usage status's entries (its own failure or hold, or one per listed datastore), the datastore_config entry and the job lists' own entries (a failure, or a 'partial:' entry for capped or unparseable rows) come earlier) -- and the cap drops the TAIL, so the block-level entries (datastores cap, job lists) always survive it. Pruning depends on errors[] only for the job lists' 'partial:' flags (see pruning_contract). Every message has the API token secret removed, including ones that quote PBS data.
errors_contract.usage: store null = /status/datastore-usage failed or is held (every total/used/avail unknown unless the per-datastore fallback read them; a scoped token never reads it); store set = PBS reported that datastore unavailable (e.g. offline maintenance), its own status read failed, or its own status answered 0/0/0 -- what PBS answers a token without the privilege at the datastore level -- and its usage reads null.
errors_contract.namespaces: That datastore's namespace listing failed, or a row of it could not be parsed (namespaces null). After an agent reload, a datastore whose walk armed the hold (each one, gathered across reloads) is walked only once the group reads reach it; until then a build's walks stop at it, and it and every datastore past it in that build's order carry 'skipped: the namespace walks stop at a datastore whose walk timed out before the agent reload, until the reads reach it after every other datastore' (namespaces null for that build, the job lists 'partial:'): every other datastore's namespaces are read first (freshness).
errors_contract.groups: (store, ns) could not be listed, or N of its rows could not be parsed; or, with ns null and a message counting them, namespaces skipped past the budget; after a read in that datastore's namespaces timed out in this build ('skipped: a read on this datastore timed out in this build, so the rest of its namespaces wait for a later one', followed by the count of namespaces not read; its remembered listing is forgotten too, until a walk lists it again, when that read waited its whole 10s read timeout); while every walk is held, in a datastore whose gc read did not answer in this build -- it timed out, is backed off or was not reached ('skipped: the namespace walks are held and the gc read of this datastore did not answer in this build, so its groups wait for one that does', followed by the count); or, when the walks did not go round every datastore, before the point the group reads resumed at in their datastore ('skipped: before the resume point of this build in its datastore, read on its next turn', followed by the count) -- all of them in unread_namespaces when that datastore's namespaces were listed this build.
errors_contract.snapshots: (store, ns) groups shipped, but some or all of their snapshot details are unknown (in_progress null on those rows): the read failed or was skipped, a row of it could not be parsed, or a last_backup was not found finished in it. When the listing did not come back as a list at all -- an HTTP error, a timeout, a reset, a budget skip, a backoff or a body that is not a list -- the namespace is in unread_namespaces too: PBS omits from /groups a group whose snapshots it failed to read, and only /snapshots fails on it (HTTP 400, like every handler error) once its scan reaches that group, so any of those may hide it. A list proves the scan ended, even with an unparseable row or a last_backup not shown finished: the namespace then stays read, and only those details are unknown.
errors_contract.sync_jobs / verify_jobs / prune_jobs: The list is null (unread), or -- message starting 'partial:' -- read but possibly missing jobs: outside the token's scope, hidden by a deeper ACL entry the agent detected (privilege_contract.deeper_acls; one below /remote flags sync_jobs only), possibly hidden by one in a datastore whose namespaces were not read in this build (or past the datastore cap), past the 200-job cap, or unparseable rows skipped.
errors_contract.cap: An array was trimmed: datastores (100; scope is then 'partial'), namespaces (1000, a total over a build's listings: the first listing of a build that alone exceeds it is kept trimmed, its namespaces null, with 'namespaces capped at 1000: N dropped'; a later listing that does not fit what is left is not kept at all, and every datastore past it that build is not even requested -- each carries 'namespaces capped at 1000: not read', namespaces null, gc and usage still shipped -- and is listed first in a later build), groups (a block-wide 5000; the namespaces trimmed or not reached are in unread_namespaces, with ns null and a count when not reached), errors (500).
errors_contract.deadline: A read skipped because its budget was spent (the tick's 20s; for the per-datastore reads -- a datastore's own status and gc -- at most half of what the walks left of it; a namespace walk -- a datastore's namespace listing, or a full-scope token's usage status -- is sent only with its whole 10s read timeout left in the tick, and past the first namespace listing of a build with 4s more beyond that; every datastore past where a build's walks stopped for lack of time carries it under 'namespaces' too) carries the message 'skipped: pbs collection deadline exceeded' under that read's own scope.
errors_contract.backoff: A read that TIMED OUT after it was sent (a read timeout that waited its whole read timeout, at least 5s; a connect timeout never reached PBS, nor did a TLS handshake that stalled, which the HTTP client reports as a read timeout) may still be running in PBS: its namespace walk never ends while a datastore's ns directory is unreadable (a stale NFS mount, EACCES, EIO), holding one PBS proxy thread for good per request -- list_namespaces does it, and so does /status/datastore-usage, which walks every datastore the token cannot audit: under a full-scope token any datastore a deeper ACL entry hides from it, which the agent cannot always see (a scoped token never reads it: it would walk every other datastore, visible to it or not) (all reproduced on PBS 4.2) -- and the proxy has one such thread per core. So those walks -- every datastore's namespace listing, and a full-scope token's usage status -- are sent only with their WHOLE read timeout (10s) left in the tick (otherwise skipped as past the budget, so a PBS merely slow late in the tick is never read as stuck), and share ONE hold: once ANY of them times out, NONE is requested again until the agent is reloaded (SIGHUP) or restarted (an agent update restarts it too) -- whatever the configuration change meanwhile (the host spelled another way, a pasted fingerprint, another token), with the message 'skipped: a namespace walk timed out and PBS may still be running it (...), so no walk (namespace listing, usage status) is sent again until the agent is reloaded (SIGHUP) -- if a datastore is broken, repair it and restart proxmox-backup-proxy first' on each of them: one broken storage pins one PBS proxy thread with its namespace walks however many datastores it carries (its other reads are bounded below), and every datastore's namespaces read null from the next build on, with walks_held true on the block (the build that armed it may still carry what it read before the timeout); the group reads go on through the listings the agent remembers (freshness). The stuck walk is a busy loop on a PBS core that logs an error each turn until proxmox-backup-proxy restarts. A reload also drops the cached block, so the next tick rebuilds it. Every other read that can take long walks no namespace (a groups listing reads one level, a datastore's own status is one statfs), so a groups or snapshot listing, a datastore's own status and its gc status are only backed off (a groups or snapshot listing that timed out also stops that build's reads of the datastore's other namespaces: errors_contract.groups): retried after one rebuild, then twice as long per further timeout, at most 6h, with the message 'skipped: this read timed out before and PBS may still be running it; retried later' -- a gc that never answers would otherwise take half of what the walks leave on every build. The two per-datastore reads still open the datastore, which on a dead hard-mounted NFS may never return either: each retry of those may pin one more PBS proxy thread, at that doubling pace. One of those two sent with less than 5s left in their half (neither one of the first datastore's two reads nor retried after a timeout) is clamped to the half instead: its timeout arms no backoff yet, but its next send gets the 5s wait and arms it (an answer within that wait is read, even past the half). The 5s wait is granted only when it leaves the group reads 3s of the tick: otherwise the read is clamped to its half, and one that timed out before is not sent at all that build (the backoff message), so a stuck read is never re-sent without its wait. While every walk is held, the groups of a datastore whose gc read did not answer in that build are not read (errors_contract.groups): on a dead storage carrying several datastores, each one's group reads would be one more pinned thread. Either way the read is unknown meanwhile, exactly like a failed read: namespaces null, the namespace in unread_namespaces, its snapshot details null, usage null (a full-scope token then reads each datastore's own status, so only estimated_full_date stays null until the reload), or that datastore's gc null.
errors_contract.datastore_config: /config/datastore could not be read: it is read only when neither the datastore listing (PBS >= 4.1.7) nor the usage status (4.1.6) names a datastore's backend. Those datastores ship backend_type null and total/used/avail/estimated_full_date null (an S3 datastore's usage measures its local cache disk, so unknown is withheld).

pve_join_contract: Agent 1.21.0+ also adds a 'pbs' object to data['proxmox'].storage rows of type 'pbs' (omitted, never null, otherwise, like 'pool'): {server, port (null = 8007), datastore, namespace ('' = root), fingerprint (lowercase, null when PVE trusts a CA-signed certificate)}. A PVE guest's backups live in the PBS group (datastore, namespace, type, vmid) of the matching PBS -- vmids alone collide when two clusters share one PBS. PBS identity: the certificate fingerprint (same spelling on both sides) plus the datastore -- join a PVE storage to the ONE reporting PBS whose fingerprint matches and which lists that datastore. A fingerprint alone is not unique (PBS VMs cloned from one template share their certificate): when two reporting PBS share it, the host breaks the tie only where it is known -- a REMOTE reporter's config['pbs']['host']:port against PVE's server:port; a loopback reporter (the recommended setup) ships no host identity -- and otherwise nothing joins. A PVE storage with no fingerprint (PVE trusts a CA-signed PBS certificate) cannot be joined yet. A guest's group may be called absent ONLY where pruning_contract makes its (datastore, namespace) authoritative in that report -- scope 'full', namespaces non-null, the namespace listed and not in unread_namespaces; anywhere else (a 'partial' scope, namespaces null, the namespace unread or not listed) the join is unknown, never 'no backups'.

healthy.description: CAPTURED from a real PBS 4.2.0 (token fivenines@pbs!monitoring with DatastoreAudit on /datastore + RemoteAudit on /remote, both propagated: the documented minimal grant), agent installed on the PBS itself (localhost, verify_ssl false: loopback). Two datastores, three namespaces each ('', 'clusterA', 'clusterA/sub'), all read (unread_namespaces []); store2 is a sync target of store1 (its snapshots carry store1's verification, copied by the sync: never verified on store2, so its groups ship verify_state/last_verified_ok null). Shows: an upload IN PROGRESS for store1 host/web01 (its snapshot listed with files [] and no size -> in_progress true, count 4, last_backup still the last FINISHED backup); a FAILED verification (store1 clusterA vm/100: a chunk was corrupted on purpose -> verify_state failed, last_verified_ok null); a newer backup never verified (store1 clusterA vm/101: verify_state null with in_progress false, last_verified_ok on the older one); client-side ENCRYPTED backups (host/db01 on both datastores and store2's vm/101 -> crypt_mode encrypt; store1 clusterA vm/101's newest backup is unencrypted -> none); a group whose only sync failed (store2 clusterA vm/100: PBS lists last-backup 0 / backup-count 0 -> last_backup null, never 1970); a pull sync job failing on a dead remote, a pull sync job failing on the corrupt chunk, a push sync job never run; GC finished WITH WARNINGS on store1 and never run on store2 (last_run_starttime null). /status/datastore-usage 'history' arrays are truncated to 3 entries (the collector does not read them).

scoped_token.description: CAPTURED: a token whose Datastore.Audit is granted on ONE namespace only (/datastore/store1/clusterA) and no Remote.Audit. PBS hides instead of refusing: /admin/datastore lists only store1, the namespace listing omits the root, verify/prune listings are EMPTY although a root-level verify and prune job exist, and /admin/datastore/{store}/status would answer total/used/avail = 0. A scoped token never reads /status/datastore-usage (to answer it PBS walks every datastore the token cannot audit), and this one audits store1 only below the datastore level, so neither is read: the /status/datastore-usage answer recorded here is the capture showing PBS omitting the keys for such a token, never requested by the agent. Hence: total/used/avail null, gc null + a 403 'gc' error, sync_jobs null + an error naming Remote.Audit, and a 'partial:' error on verify_jobs and prune_jobs so the server never reads [] as 'no job'.

Its effective privileges include Datastore.Read (a full restore of every backup) and Datastore.Modify/Prune (deleting them), so the agent refuses to use it: over_privileged envelope, nothing collected, no datastores key. PBS answers /access/permissions with {} and EVERY listing with HTTP 200 and an empty list, so an empty read proves nothing: no_datastore_access envelope, never a block of empty arrays. (A DatastoreAudit grant on /datastore WITHOUT propagation, also captured, reads {'/datastore': {'Datastore.Audit': false}} and ends the same way.)

snapshots_unreadable.description: SYNTHETIC, derived from 'healthy': the /snapshots read of store1 namespace clusterA times out (a namespace with tens of thousands of snapshots). Its groups still ship, with last_backup/count from /groups (a lower bound on PBS < 4.0.17 while an upload runs: field_contract groups[]) and every snapshot detail null -- in_progress null marks the rows as 'details unknown', never 'never verified' -- and a 'snapshots' error names (store1, clusterA). PBS never finished its scan, so a group it left out of /groups (its snapshot directory unreadable -- only /snapshots would have failed on it) could be hiding: clusterA IS in unread_namespaces, and nothing may be pruned there (pruning_contract). The timeout also stops this build's reads of store1's other namespaces (its storage could be dead): clusterA/sub is in unread_namespaces too, with a 'groups' entry counting it, until a walk lists store1 again (the next build).

older_pbs.description: SYNTHETIC, derived from 'healthy' (store1 only): a PBS that predates namespaces (2.1, 404 on the namespace endpoint -> the root namespace only), push sync (400 on sync-direction=all -> the bare /admin/sync, pull jobs only) and the GC job status (its gc body is the legacy shape: the last GC's task id and counters only -> last_run_starttime set, last_run_state null = 'not reported', not 'never ran'). Its listing names no backend (PBS < 4.1.7), so the backend comes from /config/datastore, where no backend property means a filesystem datastore -> backend_type 'filesystem' and its usage ships. Nor does it have the prune jobs API (added in 2.2, with namespaces): 404 -> prune_jobs null plus a 'prune_jobs' error -- unknown, never 'no prune jobs' (PBS 2.1 prunes on per-datastore schedules). Nothing else is an error.

first_backup_in_progress.description: CAPTURED, over 'healthy': store1's root namespace while the FIRST backup of a new group (host/fresh01) is still uploading. PBS reports that upload as the group's last-backup (backup-count 1, files [] -- it skips its finished filter for a lone snapshot), while web01's upload that was still running in 'healthy' (1790587027) has finished and is now its last_backup. The agent discards an unfinished last-backup: fresh01 ships last_backup null and in_progress true, never 'backed up'.

namespace_walk_held.description: SYNTHETIC, derived from 'healthy': the namespace listing of store1 times out (a datastore whose ns directory is unreadable: a stale NFS mount, EACCES, EIO -- PBS's namespace walk then never ends and holds one proxy thread for good). Every namespace walk is now held until the agent is reloaded: store2's namespace listing is not sent, both datastores ship namespaces null and no group (this agent remembers no listing yet: scenario namespace_walk_held_remembered shows the group reads going on over remembered ones), and the block reads walks_held: true (field_contract.walks_held). This is the build that ARMED the hold: its usage (read before the timeout) still ships; from the next build on the usage status is held too, and a full-scope token reads each datastore's own status instead (no estimated_full_date): scenario namespace_walk_held_steady. Both gcs ship: they are read after the walks, within half of what the walks left. After a reload, the reads resume past store1, and store1 is walked only once the group reads reach it, so store2 is walked and read before store1 can arm the hold again. No namespace listing was read, so the three job lists carry a 'partial:' flag.

namespace_walk_held_steady.description: SYNTHETIC, derived from 'healthy': a later build of an agent that armed the hold (namespace_walk_held) and still holds every walk (agent_state: an earlier build armed the hold; only an agent reload or restart releases it). Nothing that walks is sent: no usage status, no namespace listing. Each datastore reads its usage from its own status (/admin/datastore/{store}/status, recorded here with synthetic values) with estimated_full_date null; namespaces and unread_namespaces null; groups [] (this agent state remembers no namespace listing: scenario namespace_walk_held_remembered); the hold message under 'usage' (store null) and under 'namespaces' for each datastore; gc as usual; the three job lists flagged 'partial:' (no namespace listing read); walks_held: true -- the state field_contract.walks_held asks the server to alert on.

namespace_walk_held_remembered.description: SYNTHETIC, derived from 'healthy': the agent state of namespace_walk_held_steady (an earlier build armed the walk hold, on store1's walk), but this agent had listed store2 before the hold was armed (agent_state.listings: the namespace listings it remembers -- not store1's, forgotten when its walk timed out). Nothing that walks is sent, every datastore's namespaces and unread_namespaces are null and walks_held is true, as in namespace_walk_held_steady -- but the group reads go on through the remembered listing: every group of store2 ships as current data (last_backup, verification, in_progress...), none authoritative (namespaces null: pruning_contract), so a still-running PBS keeps reporting its backups while its namespace walks are held; store1's groups are not read until a walk lists it again.
